title: Korean Honey-Gochugaru Chicken Glaze
description: Mild gochugaru blooms in warm oil before honey and ginger turn it into a sticky red dakgangjeong-style glaze.

ingredients.name: mild ground gochugaru
ingredients.note: Choose unsalted mild Korean red pepper, finely ground.

ingredients.name: fresh garlic cloves
ingredients.note: Peel and finely grate unless the step specifies otherwise.

ingredients.name: fresh ginger juice
ingredients.note: Finely grate peeled ginger and squeeze out the juice.

ingredients.name: coconut aminos
ingredients.note: Use Coconut Secret Original at 90 mg sodium per teaspoon. Low-sodium batch: use 1 tsp total.

ingredients.name: low-sodium chicken broth
ingredients.note: Use plain homemade or unsalted carton broth at about 35 mg sodium per cup, with household-approved ingredients.

steps.title: Bloom the red pepper
steps.text: Warm {oil}, {ga} and {go} over low heat for 30 seconds. The oil should turn brick-red while the garlic stays pale.

steps.title: Make the honey glaze
steps.text: Whisk in {gi}, {ho}, {a}, {rv}, {ch} and {to} and simmer gently for 4–5 minutes until the color is uniform.

steps.title: Mix the slurry
steps.text: Stir {sl} into {cw} in a small cup until smooth.

steps.title: Thicken the sauce
steps.text: Whisk the slurry into the gently simmering base. Cook for 60–90 seconds, stirring, until the sauce coats the back of a spoon.

steps.title: Check the yield
steps.text: Measure the sauce in a heatproof cup. Aim for 1 cup. If short, loosen with a little hot sodium-free water. If over, return it to the pan and simmer briefly to the mark.

steps.title: Serve the sauce
steps.text: Fold through moist bite-sized chicken or spoon over tofu. Put additional gochugaru on the table for anyone who wants it hotter.

notes: Yield: 1 cup, or four 1/4-cup portions. Low-sodium option for the full batch: Use 1 tsp coconut aminos in place of 4 tsp. Use the same final 1-cup yield and 1/4-cup serving. Make ahead: Make the sauce the day before and portion it before chilling. Refrigerate in shallow covered portions within 2 hours and use within 3 days. Freezer-Friendly Verdict: Yes. Freeze flat in 1/4-cup portions for up to 2 months. Whisk again after thawing to restore the texture. Fridge reheat: Reheat a portion in a small pan, stirring to a brief boil and at least 165°F. Loosen with a splash of water if it tightens. Freezer reheat: Thaw overnight in the refrigerator, then use the fridge reheat method. Option A uses the listed seasonings. For a gentler Option B, use 1/8 teaspoon gochugaru and replace half the vinegar with water. Estimated nutrition per serving (1/4 of recipe): 58 kcal, 0.6 g protein, 11.8 g total carbohydrate, 1.2 g fat, 0.2 g fiber, 99 mg sodium. Low-sodium version per 1/4 cup: 54 kcal, 0.6 g protein, 10.8 g total carbohydrate, 1.2 g fat, 0.2 g fiber, 31 mg sodium. Figures cover the sauce alone. Sodium varies with brands.

steps.text: Start the enamel Dutch oven over medium-low heat for 2–3 minutes; use the lid for covered steps. Reduce heat once liquids simmer and stir across the heavy base.
